title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android: Town Hall front-of-room view control (Worldwide)

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions: default view

claims.claim: The cited sources do not describe the contents of the Town Hall front-of-room presenter view.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: The Teams admin center path is Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to **Meetings** > **Events policies**. / Select an existing policy or create a new one. / turn the **Events optimized for a large audience** toggle **On** or **Off**.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled disables large-audience event creation for that policy.
claims.quote:
### -AllowTownhalls
This setting governs if a user can create an event optimized for large audiences using Teams Events. / **Disabled**: Disables the **Optimize for Large Audience** option for organizers scheduling an event. / -Identity: Unique identifier assigned to the Teams Events policy.
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to controls[0].note: 'The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference currently describes the policy as still in preview.' The cmdlet reference states this, although the cited events management page describes the setting without a preview caveat.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Events optimized for a large audience controls whether users with that policy can create events such as Town Halls.
claims.quote: **Events optimized for a large audience** (On,Off) | `-AllowTownhalls` (Enabled,Disabled) | Controls whether users with this policy can create events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changing the event setting to Off after scheduling prevents the user from running or starting the event.
claims.quote: If you change the value to **Off** after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The event-creation policy setting does not set the Town Hall front-of-room view.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams Rooms Android town hall front-of-room view control admin policy settings AllowTownhalls TownhallEventAttendeeAccess'; read set-up-events and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy, including AllowTownhalls, and the Android release notes. No view-setting operation documented for AllowTownhalls.

claims.where: Governance controls: first sentence
claims.claim: The existing event-creation setting is the only admin control the sources tie to this scenario.
claims.quote: **Who can attend events optimized for a large audience**(Everyone,Everyone in my organization excluding guests,Everyone in my organization including guests) / Controls who can attend events optimized for large audiences (such as town halls) created by organizers with this policy.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'The existing events policy setting decides whether organisers can create Town Halls.' Keep the following sentence, 'It does not set the front-of-room view.' The cited page also documents attendance controls, so remove the exclusive claim without adding controls or coverage.

claims.where: Open questions: direct console connection
claims.claim: The resolved-issues list says Town Hall presenter support and front-of-room view control are available with direct console connection.
claims.quote: Presenter support for Teams Town Hall and Front-of-room view control for Teams Town Hall are available with direct console connection.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter and cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Rooms without Pro need the Pro licence to use this feature, but the paragraph groups that licence with indirect costs.
claims.quote: Features with ![](../media/mtr-pro-icon.png) are only available with Teams Rooms Pro license.
claims.fix: Replace 'The indirect cost is admin time to brief presenters and, for any room not on Pro, the Teams Rooms Pro licence.' with 'The indirect cost is admin time to brief presenters. A room without Teams Rooms Pro needs that licence to use this feature.' Keep the low rating as the incremental communication cost for already licensed rooms.

claims.where: front matter: action; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Action none fits a launched change that the briefing says requires presenter communication and checking organiser policies.
claims.quote: action: "none" / "the practical work is communication: tell presenters and event organisers how the room behaves" / "Check that the events policy for your organisers has the Events optimized for a large audience setting On"
claims.fix: Change action from 'none' to 'prepare': the standard uses prepare for an arriving low-risk, low-cost change requiring communication, and reserves none for awareness with nothing to configure or decide.
